h1: Cortina d'Ampezzo ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Cortina d'Ampezzo sits at 1,211 metres in a bowl of Dolomite walls that UNESCO lists as World Heritage, and the town has hosted the Olympics twice. Its own ski area counts 33 lifts and 101 slopes, and the Dolomiti Superski pass it belongs to opens 1,200 kilometres of slopes and 450 lifts across twelve linked areas.
stayOverview: The town is spread along the valley floor under the Tofane, with the cable cars leaving from its edges. Corso Italia is the pedestrian spine; the outlying hamlets are quieter and cheaper.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. The centre puts you on the Corso; the hamlets need the ski bus.
rentalCars: Cortina is reached by road over the Dolomite passes, about two hours from Venice.

season.unannounced: No 2026/27 dates are published. The lift company's winter pages still carry last season's - 5 December 2025 to 12 April 2026 - and Dolomiti Superski's table does the same. Carrying a season that has already ended would be worse than leaving the row open.

baseElevation.note: The altitude the Freccia nel Cielo cable car leaves Cortina from, on its way to Tofana di Mezzo at 3,244 m.

longestRun.note: Our pick among the Cortina lift companies' own published run lengths. Faloria Cristallo lists all 14 of its pistes with lengths, the next longest being Rio Gere at 2,556 m; on the Tofana side only Forcella Rossa carries a length, 2 km. Neither calls any run the area's longest. Cortina skiers also reach the longer Armentarola descent from the Lagazuoi, but that one ends in Alta Badia.

dayPass.note: Dolomiti Superski prices the day pass by date - early and late-season promo, season, and high season - and publishes the rate only through its own price calculator, with 5% off online two days ahead. Its 2026/27 adult season pass is EUR 990 in advance sale to 24 December and EUR 1,060 after.

facts.text: 13 black slopes, the steepest being the Forcella Rossa at a 62% maximum gradient.
Five blacks on Tofane and five on Faloria - Cristallo, on slopes that have carried World Cup and World Championship races.
20 of the 35 slopes on Tofane are graded blue, and 95% of the ski area is covered by snowmaking.
